predecessors.note: Cliopatria shares Wikidata Q12544 between 'Roman Empire' (-31..394) and 'Eastern Roman Empire' (395..632): the eastern court is the legal continuation of the undivided empire, but the 395 division is a partition (rule 7) and the roman-empire row belongs to another group, so the East gets its own dossier from 395. The colour agent may give both rows one hue (family rome).

land.text: everything: the same state continues without a break

successors.note: Cliopatria's row break at 632/633 ('Eastern Roman Empire' -> 'Byzantine Empire', Seshat tr_east_roman_emp -> tr_byzantine_emp_1) is a periodisation, not an event; rule 2 (one colour for life) asks that byzantine-empire keep this dossier's colour. The byzantine-empire dossier (sibling part) carries the Arab conquests from 633.

keyframe_review.note: 1.98 M km2 for 395: the eastern half at the division ('the Roman Empire was divided once more between his two sons'; Arcadius 'inherited the East and Constantinople'). The bbox's western edge at 14.34 E is a single Malta cell; Sirmium and Dalmatia are outside, correctly for 395. Infobox area check: 2.35 M km2 for 457 against the 455-458 shape's 1.98 M km2 (ratio 0.84).

correction.text: the 395 shape unchanged: the Hunnic raid zone (Armenia, Cappadocia, Syria to Antioch and Euphratesia, 395-398) and Alaric's Goths in Greece (395-397) and Epirus (397-401) are occupations, hatched, not losses of provinces

keyframe_review.note: 1.78 M km2: Cliopatria hands 656 cells of Armenia, Cappadocia and northern Syria to 'Huns' and 61 cells of Greece to 'Visigoths'. Both are raids, not conquests: the Huns in 395 'overran Armenia, pillaged Cappadocia, entered parts of Syria, threatened Antioch'; Alaric 'marched through Thermopylae' and sacked Athens in 396. Rule 4 draws them hatched over Roman land.

correction.text: the 395 shape unchanged; the Hunnic raid zone hatched to 398 and Epirus under Alaric's federates hatched to 401 (Greece south of Epirus is free from 397)

keyframe_review.note: 1.76 M km2 for 397-401: Greece returns but Epirus (87 cells) goes to 'Visigoths' and the Hunnic zone in Anatolia stays Hunnic. Alaric was made 'magister militum per Illyricum' by the Eastern court in 397, so his Goths in Epirus were federates on Roman soil until the province was transferred to the West in 399 and Alaric left for Italy in late 401. Review fix 2026-10-19: the ledger frees Greece in 397 ('pushed Alaric's forces north into Epirus') and ends the Hunnic occupation in 398 (Eutropius's 'defeat of a Hun invasion in 398'), three years before Cliopatria's 402 shape returns the zone.

1.97 M km2 for 402-406: the Hunnic zone is back (632 cells) but Epirus (48 cells, 19.4-21.3 E) is nobody's until 407. Alaric 'decided to invade Italy in spring 402, crossing the Alpine frontier near Aquileia' (Kulikowski), so Epirus is Roman again from 402.

1.98 M km2 for 407-438, identical to the 395 shape. The 421-422 Persian war ended 'without changes to the status quo' (Theodosius II page). Sirmium (Pannonia Secunda), recognised as Eastern in 437, is not in the shape; the ledger adds it for 437-441.

correction.text: the shape as drawn plus Sirmium, the prefecture's seat from 437 until the Huns took it in 441

keyframe_review.note: 439-440 differs from 407 by 149 km2 of noise. Valentinian III 'recognized Eastern sovereignty over the prefecture' of Illyricum as part of Licinia Eudoxia's dowry (married 29 October 437) and 'the capital reportedly moved to Sirmium (437-441)'; Cliopatria never gives Sirmium to the East.

441-442: five Danube cells at Singidunum, Margus and Viminacium (20-21 E) pass to 'Hunnic Empire': 'The Huns invaded the Balkans in 441, sacking Margus and Viminacium, then taking Singidunum and Sirmium.' The bbox's jump from 14.34 E to 18.81 E is the Malta cell dropping out for these two years (back in 443): noise, not an event.

correction.text: the shape as drawn, right from 447/448; for 443-446 the 441 shape (the strip still Roman, the fighting zone contested)

keyframe_review.note: 443-450, 1.95 M km2: 85 cells of northern Moesia and Thrace (22.9-27.4 E, 41.2-43.9 N) pass to the Huns. The Utus page describes the buffer zone that 'extended 300 miles from Singidunum to Novae', '100 miles or five days' journey south of the Danube', under the treaty 'signed in the fall of 447' or 'in 448'; the Theodosius II page dates Anatolius's treaty '443 or 447'. Cliopatria's 443 is the earlier of the two dates for a strip that the sources attach to the 447 peace.

451: the strip and the Danube cities return (93 cells). 'All Eastern Roman tributary payments to Attila ceased under Marcian while Attila was busy invading Italy' and Marcian 'launched preemptive expeditions across the Danube into the Hunnic heartland'; Attila was in Gaul in 451 (Attila page).
452-454: identical to 407 within three cells of noise (Cyrenaica, Crete, Levant).

455-458, 1.98 M km2: 26 cells along the Danube's south bank from Singidunum to the delta (20.6-28.1 E) are added, the river line re-established after Attila died in 453 and the Huns 'quickly collapsed' at Nedao in 454. Infobox 2.35 M km2 for 457 (ratio 0.84, fine).
459-468: one cell on the Montenegrin coast added, removed again in 469: noise. The 468 expedition against the Vandals (Cape Bon) moved no border.

469-489, 2.00 M km2: 75 cells of the southern Crimea (32.8-35.3 E, 44.5-46.0 N: Cherson and the coast) are added when Cliopatria's Hunnic Empire shrinks to a residue; 'In 469, Dengizich was defeated and killed in Thrace.' The Chersonesus page says only that the city, 'captured by the Huns' in the 370s, 'became a Byzantine possession during the Early Middle Ages' and withstood a Göktürk siege in 581: the year is Cliopatria's (ledger confidence 1). Nothing marks the end of the West in 476: Italy and Dalmatia are Odoacer's, then Theodoric's, as the ledger's vassal tint. Review 2026-10-19: the Bosporan Kingdom page has the Gothic Bosporan realm regaining its independence in the 450s-460s and imperial control only after the 527 revolt; the Dengizich page never mentions the Crimea. No page gives the empire these cells in 469, so the ledger takes them from 'nobody' at confidence 1 and the shape stays Cliopatria's, unverified.

490-509: identical to 469 within three cells. Theodoric's Goths, federates in 'Dacia Ripensis and Moesia Inferior' 483-488, left for Italy in autumn 488 (ledger vassal tint). The Anastasian War (502-506) ended 'Status quo ante bellum': Amida's loss (502/503) and recovery (504) are ledger occupation events inside this shape.

510-522, 1.97 M km2: 54 cells of Palaestina Tertia (the Negev, Sinai and the Arabah, 34.6-36.4 E, 28.1-31.3 N) go to Cliopatria's new 'Ghassanids' row (946 cells, mostly desert that was never drawn Roman), and 74 cells of the Danube bank between Singidunum and Ratiaria (20.0-23.2 E) to 'Kingdom of the Gepids'. The Ghassanid land is vassal tint (foederati 'controlling parts of Palestine' from the 473 treaty; al-Harith's elevation 529); the Gepid strip has no page behind it before the Gepids 'settl[ed] around Singidunum' after 537 (ledger confidence 1).

523-533: three cells of noise added. The Iberian War (526-532) ended with the Perpetual Peace of September 532: 'all territories seized during the war by either side were returned'; Iberia Persian, Lazica Roman.

534-535, 2.19 M km2: Africa (Zeugitana, Byzacena, Tripolitania), Sardinia, Corsica, the Balearics and Septem (the bbox reaches -6.0 E) from the Vandal Kingdom, 745 cells. Carthage fell 15 September 533, Gelimer surrendered in March 534, the prefecture was created in April 534. The Moorish interior (Numidia, the Mauretanias) is drawn Roman although 'inland Numidia and Mauretania stayed largely under Mauri control' until John Troglita's victory of 548: soft, contested (ledger). Sicily is still Gothic (Palermo fell late December 535), rightly.

536-539, 2.31 M km2: Sicily (535), Dalmatia ('all Dalmatia by late June' 536) and southern Italy to about 41.6 N (Naples November, Rome December 536) added, 442 cells. Rome sits on the edge (2 of 7 cells), fair for a city besieged March 537 to March 538.

correction.text: the shape as drawn with northern Syria and the Mesopotamian frontier restored (the land the Sasanian 540 shape takes from the 536 shape), and without the Verona and Brescia districts, Gothic until 562

keyframe_review.note: 540-545, 2.33 M km2: Ravenna (May 540) and the Po valley added (504 cells), but Cliopatria also moves 419 cells of northern Syria and Mesopotamia (Aleppo, half of Antioch's cells, 35-45 E) to the Sasanian Empire for 540-545. Khosrow 'invaded Syria, destroyed Antioch' in 540 but 'withdrew after extorting money from Syrian and Mesopotamian cities': a raid and a contested frontier (ledger), not a Persian province. The shape also gives the empire Verona and Brescia, which the Goths held until 562.

correction.text: the shape as drawn without the Verona and Brescia districts (Gothic until 562)

keyframe_review.note: 546-554, 2.40 M km2: Totila's reconquest removes 149 cells of central and southern Italy (Naples 543, Rome 17 December 546, Rome again 549/550) and the Syrian cells return after the five-year truce of 545. Verona and Brescia are again drawn Roman.

correction.text: the shape as drawn without the Verona and Brescia districts, 'subjugated in 562'; Lazica inside the shape is vassal land (tint)

keyframe_review.note: 555-560, 2.56 M km2: Spania (312 cells, 'the Baetica coast from Malaga to the mouth of the Guadalete, plus the southern parts of Carthaginiensis'), Italy after Taginae (552) and Mons Lactarius (October 553), the Gepid Danube bank and eastern Lazica (56 cells of Colchis) added. Spania is dated 555 by Cliopatria (the second force 'landed at Cartagena in early March 555'); the first landing was June/July 552. The Spanish shape is generous for a province that 'never extended very far inland', but no page gives a line.

561-566, 2.60 M km2, Cliopatria's largest shape: the rest of northern Italy (Verona and Brixia 'were subjugated in 562', one year early) and 38 more cells of Lazica/Suania after the Fifty-Year Peace of 562; 15 cells at the Danube mouth go to the new 'Avar Khaganate' row. Infobox 3.4 M km2 for 565 (ratio 0.77); the Justinian dynasty page's 'around 2.7 million km2' gives 0.96. Lazica is vassal tint.

correction.text: the shape as drawn plus Sirmium (Roman 567-582) and plus the Asidona coast until 572; the 'Georgia' cells are Lazica, vassal tint

keyframe_review.note: 567-568, 2.58 M km2: 96 cells of Lazica (40-43 E) move to Cliopatria's 'Georgia' row (567-576), which is the same client kingdom under another name (the georgia owner should treat 567-576 as Lazica, vassal of this empire), and 16 cells of the Guadalete coast go to the Visigoths five years before Leovigild's capture of Asidona (572). 'After 567, Sirmium was returned to the East Roman Empire' when the Gepid kingdom fell; Cliopatria omits it.

correction.text: the shape as drawn plus Sirmium (Roman until 582) and, until 572, the Asidona coast

keyframe_review.note: 569-576, 2.48 M km2: 374 cells of northern Italy to 'Lombards': Alboin crossed from Pannonia in spring 568, Milan fell in 569, Pavia in 572 after a three-year siege. Sirmium still omitted.

correction.text: the 569-576 eastern frontier restored minus Dara (Persian 573-591), Sirmium kept until its fall in 582, Naples Roman; otherwise as drawn

keyframe_review.note: 577-586, 2.38 M km2: the duchies of Spoleto (57 cells) and Benevento (130 cells, including three of Naples' four cells, which stayed Roman) are carved out (Benevento's infobox says 'Established: 577'); 129 cells of Spania go to Leovigild (Asidona 572, Cordoba 572, the Orospeda); 137 cells from Sophene to the Tigris go to Persia and 97 cells of Lazica return from 'Georgia'. The eastern strip is the zone of Khosrow I's 575 raid ('sacked Sebasteia but failed to take Theodosiopolis') and of the Mesopotamian truce front, not a conquest: the only fortress Persia held was Dara (573-591), which Cliopatria never removes.

correction.text: the shape as drawn without Dara (Persian 573-591) and Martyropolis (Persian 589-591)

keyframe_review.note: 587-591, 2.41 M km2: Cliopatria returns 97 of the eastern cells (Sophene, Arzanene, the Tur Abdin) in 587, between Solachon (586) and the fall of Martyropolis 'through the treachery of Sittas' (589); Dara stays drawn Roman though Persian until 591.

592-601, 2.53 M km2: 513 cells of Persarmenia and western Iberia (Yerevan, Ani, Kars, Mtskheta near Tbilisi) added, the price of Khosrow II's restoration in 591: 'Khosrow II gives the Byzantine Empire most of Persian Armenia and western half of Iberia'. Nine Spanish cells go to the Visigoths ('it extended no further north than the Sierra Nevada' by the year 600, Spania page).

correction.text: as drawn until 604; from 604 without Dara and, by 610, without Roman Mesopotamia and Armenia (the land Cliopatria's 612 shape gives Persia)

keyframe_review.note: 602-611, 2.53 M km2: 35 cells of the Po valley to the Lombards (Agilulf: Parma, Piacenza, Padua, Cremona, Mantua 'within the decade up to 603'). The east is unchanged although Dara fell in 604 'after a nine-month siege', Mardin and Amida in 609, Theodosiopolis in 609/610 and Edessa in 610: Cliopatria moves them to Persia only in 612.

correction.text: as drawn until 613; from the Battle of Antioch (613) without Syria and from 614 without Palestine (the Levant), Persian until 629

keyframe_review.note: 612-616, 2.31 M km2: 816 cells of Mesopotamia, Armenia and Cilicia to Persia. The shape keeps Antioch, Damascus and Jerusalem until 617, but Heraclius lost the Battle of Antioch in 613 and 'Damascus, Apamea and Emesa fall'; Jerusalem fell in 614 'after a three-week siege'.

correction.text: as drawn without the Levant remnants; Egypt removed from June 619 (Alexandria) and wholly by 621

keyframe_review.note: 617-622, 1.88 M km2: Syria, Palestine, central Anatolia (Chalcedon 617, Ancyra 620/622; Kayseri gone, Ankara 2 of 10 cells), Lazica and Iberia to Persia (1,370 cells) and the Balkan interior from Naissus to Serdica (231 cells, taken 615) to the Avars. Egypt stays drawn Roman until 623 although Alexandria was betrayed to the Persians in June 619 and 'By 621 the province was securely in Persian hands'. The shape also keeps 149 Levant cells (half of Judaea) that were Persian from 613-614.

correction.text: the shape as drawn without the Naissus-Serdica interior (Avar/Slav since 615)

keyframe_review.note: 623-625, 1.23 M km2, the nadir: Egypt (2,118 cells) and Spania (157 cells, Cartagena 624, 'save the Balearic Islands') gone. Cliopatria also returns 104 cells of the Naissus-Serdica interior (22-24 E, 42-44 N) to the empire in 623, when its Avar row shrinks; the Avars had captured 'Naissus and Serdica' in 615 and no page returns them. Rhodes (fallen 622/623) is still drawn Roman: ledger occupation.

correction.text: the 623 shape without Avar-occupied Thrace (hatched for the summer), plus Lazica and western Iberia as vassal/allied land; Persarmenia and Atropatene contested

keyframe_review.note: 626, 1.41 M km2: the Avars take 69 cells of Thrace up to the walls (siege 29 June to 7/8 August 626), while Cliopatria adds 801 cells of Armenia, Lazica, Iberia and Mesopotamia: Heraclius 'sacks Dvin' (624), 'captures Amida and Martyropolis' (625), winters in Caucasian Albania. Lazica and western Iberia were the empire's clients and allies ('the Laz, together with the Abasgians, took part in Heraclius' campaigns'); Armenia and Atropatene are a campaign zone, contested with Persia 624-628 (blend), not territory.

correction.text: the shape as drawn without the Levant cells it adds in 627 (Persian-held until 629)

keyframe_review.note: 627, 1.72 M km2: Anatolia (Kayseri, Ankara, the Bosporus shore) and Thrace return, rightly (Shahrbaraz's army left Chalcedon; he 'disobeyed and camped at Ardashir Khurrah' in 627; Nineveh 12 December 627). But 394 cells of northern Syria also return, although Shahrbaraz's army held Syria, Palestine and Egypt until 'in the summer of 629 the Persian troops began leaving Egypt' (Sasanian conquest of Egypt page).

correction.text: the shape as drawn without the Levant cells added since 626 (evacuated by the Persians in 629)

keyframe_review.note: 628, 1.73 M km2: 55 more cells of Mesopotamia (Amida) added after Kavad II's peace of February 628, in which 'The Byzantines regained all lost territories'; Syria still drawn Roman a year early.

629, 2.45 M km2: Egypt, Palestine and Syria return (2,450 cells) as the Persians evacuate ('in the summer of 629 the Persian troops began leaving Egypt'); 43 cells of the Mesopotamian frontier go back to Persia, the pre-war line ('Status quo ante bellum'). The True Cross was restored to Jerusalem on 21 March 630 (or 629).

630-632, 2.35 M km2: 346 cells of the Balkan interior (Macedonia, Epirus, Dardania, inland Greece; 18-24 E, 38-44 N) pass to nobody, Cliopatria's rendering of the Slavic settlement: the prefecture of Illyricum lost 'most of the Balkan hinterland' to Slavic incursions in the 630s, 'Byzantine control remained only in parts of Thrace near Constantinople, Thessalonica and its environs, and some coastal strips in Greece'. Four Caucasus cells go to Khazaria. The next shape (633) belongs to Cliopatria's 'Byzantine Empire' row, the same state.

region.text: Lazica (Egrisi), the kingdom around Archaeopolis and Phasis

ledger.note: 395: Lazica, the empire's client kingdom on the Black Sea. Infobox 'vassal of Roman Empire: 2nd to 5th century'; 'The division of the Roman Empire in 395 enabled Lazica to strengthen and expand'; its kings 'did not pay tribute or provide military support' but were installed from Constantinople (Tzath I 'in 523'). Cliopatria keeps a separate Lazica row to 545; this event tints it as a vassal (rule 4).

region.text: Armenia, Cappadocia and northern Syria to Antioch and Euphratesia: the cells Cliopatria's 396 Huns shape takes from the 395 empire

ledger.note: 395: the Huns pour through the Caucasus. 'The Huns began their first large-scale attack on the Eastern Roman Empire in 395': they 'overran Armenia, pillaged Cappadocia, entered parts of Syria, threatened Antioch, and passed through Euphratesia'. Cliopatria hands the land to 'Huns' for 396-401; drawn hatched over Roman territory instead (rule 4).

region.text: Thessaly, central Greece, Attica and the Peloponnese (395-397)

ledger.note: 395: Alaric's Goths rise and march on Greece. 'Alaric rebelled again' after Theodosius's death (17 January 395); his forces 'went down to Athens and the coast', in 396 he 'marched through Thermopylae' and sacked Athens, plundering 'as far south as the Peloponnese'; Stilicho pushed him 'north into Epirus', where in 397 Eutropius made him 'magister militum per Illyricum'. A roving federate army on Roman soil, hatched. Review fix 2026-10-19: region narrowed to Greece south of Epirus; Epirus is a separate occupation from 397 (see the 397 events).

region.text: the praetorian prefectures of the East and of Illyricum (the dioceses of Dacia and Macedonia), Cliopatria's 395 shape

ledger.note: 395: Theodosius dies; Arcadius rules the East from Constantinople. 'In 395 the Roman Empire was divided once more between his two sons': Arcadius 'inherited the East and Constantinople, and Honorius inherited the West'; Arcadius reigned from 17 January 395 (emperor list). The prefecture of Illyricum 'took its permanent form, incorporating Macedonia and Dacia with Thessalonica as its capital' (Illyricum page).

region.text: Thessaly, central Greece, Attica and the Peloponnese

ledger.note: 397: Alaric's Goths are out of Greece. After the sack of Athens (396) Stilicho 'pushed Alaric's forces north into Epirus', and in 397 Eutropius 'established Alaric as magister militum per Illyricum' (Alaric I page, re-read 2026-10-19). Greece south of Epirus is free of his army from 397; Epirus is hatched from 397 to 401 (next events). Review fix: the first version hatched Greece for four years too many.

region.text: Epirus

ledger.note: 397: Alaric's Goths hold Epirus. Stilicho 'pushed Alaric's forces north into Epirus' and in 397 Eutropius 'established Alaric as magister militum per Illyricum' (Alaric I page, re-read 2026-10-19); in 399 the Eastern regime 'nominally transferred Alaric's province to the West'. Cliopatria's 397 shape gives Epirus (87 cells) to 'Visigoths'. A federate army on Roman soil, hatched, until it leaves for Italy (401).

region.text: Armenia, Cappadocia and northern Syria

ledger.note: 398: the Hunnic raiders are beaten. 'Eutropius' ascension to power was assisted by his defeat of a Hun invasion in 398' (Eutropius page, 2026-10-19), which closes the raid that began in 395. The page does not name the land or say how the Huns left, so the zone is the one Cliopatria hands to the Huns in 396. Cliopatria keeps it Hunnic to 401 and returns it in 402; the occupation ends here, three years before the shape does (the 396 keyframe already read 395-398). Review fix: the first version had 401 at confidence 1. huns.json /ledger/5 closes the same occupation in 396 (also confidence 1) and should adopt 398.

region.text: Epirus

ledger.note: 401: Alaric leaves Epirus for Italy. In 399 'the Eastern regime transferred Alaric's province to the West, removing his Roman rank'; 'Alaric's attack began in late 401' (Halsall) or he 'decided to invade Italy in spring 402, crossing the Alpine frontier near Aquileia' (Kulikowski). Cliopatria's 'Visigoths' row moves to Italy in 402. Review fix 2026-10-19: narrowed to Epirus, the land of the 397 occupation_start; Greece south of it was freed in 397.

region.text: Castra Martis in Dacia Ripensis and the Thracian diocese north of the Haemus

ledger.note: 408: Uldin crosses the Danube. 'In the summer of 408, the Huns learned that Stilicho would not push Alaric I's Visigoths into Illyricum' and 'entered the Balkans and Thrace'; 'The Huns captured Castra Martis in Dacia Ripensis' (Uldin page, re-read 2026-10-19). Only that fort is named as taken; the zone is the huns dossier's Moesia (huns.json /ledger/6), hatched, not annexed. The page gives a season, not a month.

region.text: Castra Martis and Dacia Ripensis

ledger.note: 409: Uldin driven back. He 'was forced to re-cross the Danube by March 23, 409' (Uldin page); the date is a 'by', so March is an upper bound. Mirrors huns.json /ledger/7.

region.text: Sirmium and Pannonia Secunda

ledger.note: 437: the West recognises Eastern Illyricum; Sirmium becomes the prefecture's seat. 'As part of the dowry of Licinia Eudoxia, Valentinian III recognized Eastern sovereignty over the prefecture. The capital reportedly moved to Sirmium (437-441)'; the marriage was on 29 October 437 (Theodosius II page). Only Sirmium's district changes hands; Dacia and Macedonia were already Eastern. Cliopatria never draws Sirmium Eastern.

region.text: Sirmium, Singidunum, Margus and Viminacium on the middle Danube

ledger.note: 441: Attila takes the Danube cities. 'The Huns invaded the Balkans in 441, sacking Margus and Viminacium, then taking Singidunum and Sirmium'; 'In 441 the Huns conquered Sirmium' (Sirmium page). Cliopatria's 441 shape drops the five cells at Singidunum, Margus and Viminacium.

region.text: the Danube provinces and Thrace from Singidunum to Naissus, Serdica, Marcianople and Athyra

ledger.note: 441-449: Attila's wars in the Balkans. The Huns 'pushed as far as Naissus (Nis) and Serdica (Sofia) and sacked nearly all the major cities on the middle Danube' (441), used 'battering rams and siege towers at Ratiara and Naissus' (443), and in 447 defeated the Romans at the Utus, 'destroyed Serdica, and reached Athyra' near Constantinople and Thermopylae (Theodosius II page). The fighting zone is the blend (rule 6).

region.text: the Moesian and Thracian bank of the Danube from Ratiaria to Novae and Marcianople, Cliopatria's 443-450 removal

ledger.note: 447: after the Utus, a strip south of the Danube is left to the Huns. The buffer zone 'extended 300 miles from Singidunum to Novae' and '100 miles or five days' journey south of the Danube' under the treaty 'signed in the fall of 447' or 'a year later in 448', with '6,000 lbs of gold up front and 2,100 lbs annually'. Cliopatria removes the strip from 443 (keyframe note: the Theodosius II page dates Anatolius's treaty '443 or 447').

region.text: the Danube provinces and Thrace

ledger.note: 449: peace with Attila. 'The war ended in 449 with an agreement for an annual tribute of 2,100 pounds of gold' (the Utus page dates the treaty to autumn 447 or 448). Attila turned west in 451.

region.text: the Danube strip from Singidunum to Novae and the cities of Singidunum, Margus and Viminacium

ledger.note: 451: the Danube frontier recovered while Attila is in Gaul. 'All Eastern Roman tributary payments to Attila ceased under Marcian while Attila was busy invading Italy'; Marcian 'launched preemptive expeditions across the Danube into the Hunnic heartland and won significant victories there'. Attila 'marched into Belgica in 451' (Attila page) and died in 453. Cliopatria restores the strip and the Danube cities in 451.

region.text: the south bank of the Danube from Singidunum to the delta

ledger.note: 455: the Danube bank re-established after the Huns' collapse. Attila died 'in the early months of 453'; at Nedao in 454 'the Hunnic Empire quickly collapsed'; Marcian 'settled formerly Hunnic vassal tribes within Eastern lands as foederati' (Theodosian page) and granted the Gepids 'an annual subsidy of 100 pounds of gold' (Gepids page). Cliopatria adds the river cells in 455.

region.text: Thrace and the lower Danube, where Dengizich pressed for land and subsidies

ledger.note: 467: Dengizich crosses the Danube. 'In 467, Dengizich crossed the frozen Danube'; Leo I replied that 'he was ready to do everything if they came to him and offered him obedience'; 'the war dragged on for two years' (Dengizich page, 2026-10-19). The page does not describe the ground the Huns held beyond the fighting in Thrace; the zone is the one huns.json uses (/ledger/19). Review fix: the first version had no Dengizich war.

region.text: Dacia Ripensis and Moesia Inferior

region.text: the south bank of the Danube from Singidunum to Ratiaria (20.0-23.2 E), 74 cells

region.text: the frontier from Lazica and Armenia to Dara and Callinicum

region.text: Zeugitana and Byzacena, the Vandal heartland around Carthage

ledger.note: 615: Sisebut takes Malaga. 'He carried out two expeditions, in 614 and 615, and conquered Malaga before 619.'

region.text: Cappadocia, Galatia and Bithynia to Chalcedon, the Anatolian cells Cliopatria's 617 shape removes

ledger.note: 617: Chalcedon and central Anatolia. 'Persians reach Chalcedon' (615); 'Chalcedon falls to Shahin' (617); 'Ancyra is captured' (620 or 622); 'Rhodes and other eastern Aegean islands fall' (622/623). Cliopatria's 617 shape removes Cappadocia, Galatia and the Bosporus shore.

region.text: Lazica

ledger.note: 617: Lazica overrun. Cliopatria's 617-625 shapes give Colchis and western Iberia to Persia; the Lazica page says only that the Persians 'won in Armenia and the Caucasus' and that the Laz 'took part in Heraclius' campaigns' in the 620s. The year is Cliopatria's. Re-read 2026-10-19: the Lazica page has no Persian conquest or hold of Lazica in the 610s-620s (only that Svaneti 'remained under Persian influence for some time' after 562).

region.text: Lazica and the western Iberian districts ceded in 591

ledger.note: 617: Lazica and western Iberia under Persian control (Cliopatria's year, confidence 1); recovered in Heraclius's Caucasian campaigns of 624-626. Re-read 2026-10-19: the Lazica page has no Persian hold of Lazica in the 610s-620s, and the war of 602-628 page gives no year for Persian operations in Lazica, Colchis or Iberia; the year stays Cliopatria's (confidence 1).

region.text: Egypt from Alexandria to the Thebaid

ledger.note: 619: Egypt. The Persian invasion began in 617 or 618; 'a man named Peter betrayed the city to the Persians in June 619' (Alexandria, per the Khuzistan Chronicle); 'By 621 the province was securely in Persian hands'; Shahrbaraz 'ruled Egypt from Alexandria for about ten years'. Cliopatria removes Egypt only in 623.

region.text: Rhodes and the eastern Aegean islands

ledger.note: 623: Rhodes. 'Rhodes and other eastern Aegean islands fall' (622/623). Cliopatria keeps Rhodes Roman; hatched until the peace of 628. Rhodes page (2026-10-19): 'In 622/3, during the climactic Byzantine-Sasanian War of 602-628, Rhodes was captured by the Sasanian navy.'

region.text: the last Spanish coast from Cartagena westward, without the Balearic Islands

ledger.note: 624: Spania ends. 'In 621 the Byzantines still held a few towns, but Suinthila recovered them shortly. By 624 the province was in Visigothic hands save the Balearic Islands'; 'The Visigoths recaptured Cartagena, capital of the province of Spania' (Heraclius page). Cliopatria's year is 623; the Balearics stay imperial.

region.text: Lazica

ledger.note: 626: Lazica with Heraclius. 'The Laz, together with the Abasgians, took part in Heraclius' campaigns against the Persians' in the 620s; Heraclius 'winters in Caucasian Albania' (624-625) and allies with the Western Turks (626), who besiege Tiflis in 627. Cliopatria restores Colchis and western Iberia to the empire in 626 (as direct land; tint here).

region.text: Lazica and the western Iberian districts

ledger.note: 626: Lazica and western Iberia recovered in the Caucasian campaigns. Heraclius 'left Constantinople again' on 25 March 624 'and campaigned in the Caucasus, winning a series of victories'; 'Göktürks under Ziebel invaded Persian Transcaucasia' (627). Cliopatria's 626 shape also adds Persarmenia and Mesopotamia, which the keyframe treats as contested, not held. Review fix 2026-10-19: the Heraclius quote names neither Lazica nor Iberia, the war of 602-628 page gives no year for operations there, and the Lazica page puts the Laz in Heraclius' campaigns only 'in the 620s'; the year 626 and the land are Cliopatria's, so confidence 1 (was 2).

region.text: Thrace from the Long Walls to the Theodosian Walls

ledger.note: 626: the Avars before Constantinople. 'The siege began on June 29, 626'; 'about 80,000 Avars and Sclaveni' against 12,000 defenders; Shahrbaraz's army at Chalcedon. Thrace up to the walls is Avar-held for the summer (Cliopatria's 626 shape removes 69 cells).

region.text: Thrace

ledger.note: 626: the siege fails. 'On 7 August, the Byzantine fleet destroyed Persian rafts, and the Sclaveni boats were rammed and destroyed. The Avar land assaults on 6-7 August were repelled'; 'the Avars retreated within two days'. 'After the failed siege, the Avars declined.'

region.text: the Danube provinces, Thrace and Macedonia

ledger.note: 626: the Avar war for the Balkans ends with the failed siege. 'After the failed siege, the Avars declined'; the khaganate stopped being a danger to Constantinople, the Balkan interior stays in Slav hands ('nobody', ledger 630). The contest blend over the Danube provinces, Thrace and Macedonia closes here.

region.text: Cappadocia, Galatia, Bithynia and the Bosporus shore, the Anatolian cells Cliopatria's 627 shape restores

ledger.note: 627: Anatolia free of Persian armies. Shahrbaraz's army was 'stationed at Chalcedon' in 626; in 627 Khosrow 'ordered him to bring his army to Ctesiphon. He disobeyed and camped at Ardashir Khurrah' (Shahrbaraz page); Heraclius 'invades the Iranian heartland' in mid-September and wins at Nineveh on 12 December 627. Cliopatria returns Anatolia in 627.

region.text: Rhodes and the eastern Aegean islands

ledger.note: 628: Rhodes returned under the peace, which restored 'all lost territories'; no page dates the island's handover. Re-read 2026-10-19: the Rhodes page is silent on the return (its next dated entry is the Umayyad occupation of 654) and the war of 602-628 page gives no year for the restoration of territory; confidence stays 1.

region.text: the Roman-Persian frontier

ledger.note: 628: Khosrow II overthrown; Kavad II makes peace. Heraclius 'plunders Dastagird' after an ultimatum of 6 January 628; 'Khosrow II is overthrown and killed, and his son Kavad II seeks peace' (February 628, Shahrbaraz page); 'The Byzantines regained all lost territories and their captured soldiers', a war indemnity and the True Cross. Infobox: 'Status quo ante bellum'.

region.text: Egypt, Palestine, Syria and the Mesopotamian and Armenian provinces, Cliopatria's 629 addition

ledger.note: 629: Syria, Palestine, Egypt, Mesopotamia and Armenia evacuated by the Persians. Shahrbaraz 'was ordered to leave Egypt but refused. Heraclius then offered to help him take the Persian throne, and an agreement followed. In the summer of 629 the Persian troops began leaving Egypt'; Heraclius 'returns the True Cross to Jerusalem' on 21 March 630 (or 629). Cliopatria restores the provinces in its 629 shape (Anatolia and northern Syria already in 627-628, the frontier strip at Nisibis back to Persia).

region.text: the Ghassanid phylarchate, Cliopatria's 629 shape

ledger.note: 629: the Ghassanid phylarchate restored with Syria. Cliopatria's Ghassanid row resumes in 629; the page has them at Nineveh (627) and defeated at the Yarmuk (636) under Jabala ibn al-Ayham (632-638), 'vassal of the Eastern Roman Empire' (infobox). The relation lasts to the dossier's end and continues in byzantine-empire. Re-read 2026-10-19: the page is silent on a resumption in 629; the improvement under Heraclius ('relations with the Ghassanids dramatically improved') is undated.

region.text: Macedonia, Epirus, Dardania and inland Greece, Cliopatria's 630 removal; Thessalonica, Athens and the coasts remain

ledger.note: 630: the Balkan interior passes to the Slavs. The prefecture of Illyricum lost 'most of the Balkan hinterland' to 'Slavic incursions' in the 630s (infobox); 'Byzantine control remained only in parts of Thrace near Constantinople, Thessalonica and its environs, and some coastal strips in Greece'. The Sclaveni page: by 615 'the whole Balkans was regarded as Sklavinia'; Slavs 'raided the western Peloponnese, Attica, and Epirus' by 586; the Croats and Serbs arrived under Heraclius (610-641). Stateless land, grey (rule 8), until the Bulgars (681) and the sclaviniae' submission; Cliopatria's year is 630.

region.text: the whole empire of 632: Anatolia, Thrace, Thessalonica and the Greek coasts, the Aegean, Syria, Palestine, Egypt, Cyrenaica, Africa, Sardinia, Corsica, the Balearics, Italy's exarchate, Sicily and Dalmatia's coast

ledger.note: 632: the dossier hands over; the state continues. Cliopatria's 'Eastern Roman Empire' row ends in 632 and its 'Byzantine Empire' row begins in 633, a periodisation of Seshat's, not an event: Heraclius reigns to 641 and the Arab wars begin 'in 633' (Heraclian page). Everything passes to byzantine-empire, which should keep this colour (rule 2). Lazica and the Ghassanids remain its vassals.

wars.name: Hunnic invasion of 395

zones.text: Armenia, Cappadocia, Syria to Antioch, Euphratesia

wars.outcome: A raid through the Caucasus: the Huns 'overran Armenia, pillaged Cappadocia, entered parts of Syria, threatened Antioch, and passed through Euphratesia'; no land changed hands. Eutropius's 'defeat of a Hun invasion in 398' (Eutropius page) closes it; Cliopatria keeps the zone Hunnic to 401.
wars.note: Review fix 2026-10-19: end moved from 401 to 398 (Eutropius page).

wars.name: Alaric's revolt in Greece and Illyricum

zones.text: Thessaly, Attica, the Peloponnese (395-397), Epirus (397-401)

wars.outcome: Alaric sacked Athens (396), was driven into Epirus by Stilicho, made magister militum per Illyricum by the East (397), lost his province when it was transferred to the West (399) and invaded Italy in late 401/402. No land ceded.

wars.name: Uldin's invasion of Thrace

zones.text: Castra Martis in Dacia Ripensis and the Thracian diocese north of the Haemus

wars.outcome: In the summer of 408 the Huns 'entered the Balkans and Thrace' and 'captured Castra Martis in Dacia Ripensis'; Uldin 'was forced to re-cross the Danube by March 23, 409'. No land changed hands.

wars.name: Roman-Sasanian War of 421-422
wars.outcome: 'ended in an indecisive stalemate'; peace in 422 'without changes to the status quo' as the Huns menaced Constantinople; a ban on new frontier fortifications (Roman-Persian Wars page).
wars.note: The war's own Wikipedia page was not opened; the Theodosius II and Roman-Persian Wars pages carry it.

wars.name: Roman-Sasanian War of 440
wars.outcome: 'Yazdegerd II raided Roman Armenia' in 440; the page states no outcome. No border moved.
wars.note: Both titles tried for the war's own page ('Roman–Sasanian War of 440', 'Roman–Sasanian War (440)') returned not found.

wars.name: Hunnic wars of Attila

zones.text: the Danube provinces and Thrace to Naissus, Serdica, Marcianople, Athyra and Thermopylae

wars.outcome: The Huns took Sirmium, Singidunum, Margus and Viminacium (441), Ratiaria and Naissus (443), won at the Utus and destroyed Marcianople and Serdica (447); the peace of 447/448 (or 449) cost 6,000 pounds of gold, 2,100 a year, and a strip 'five days' journey south of the Danube' from Singidunum to Novae. Marcian stopped the tribute (450), Attila went west (451), died (453); Nedao (454).
wars.note: Dates disagree: the Theodosius II page gives Anatolius's treaty '443 or 447', the Huns page ends the war in 449, the Utus page dates the strip treaty to autumn 447 or 448. Cliopatria removes the strip 443-450.

wars.name: Dengizich's war on the Danube

zones.text: Thrace and the lower Danube

wars.outcome: Dengizich crossed the frozen Danube in 467; Leo I answered that 'he was ready to do everything if they came to him and offered him obedience'; 'the war dragged on for two years'; Dinzirichus 'was killed by Anagastes, general in Thrace' in 469 and the Hun state ends. The page reports no land ceded either way.
wars.note: The Bassianae siege (c. 468, against the Ostrogoths) is in huns.json's version of the war and is outside the empire's land.

wars.name: Vandal expedition of 468
wars.outcome: 'the most ambitious campaign ever launched against the Vandal state': at Cape Bon 'the Vandals destroyed the Western fleet and part of the Eastern fleet using fire ships'. Gaiseric concluded a 'perpetual peace' with Constantinople in 476. No border moved; Africa 'would remain outside of imperial control until the reign of Justinian' (Leonid page).

wars.name: Anastasian War

zones.text: Theodosiopolis, Martyropolis, Amida; Edessa besieged in vain (503)

wars.outcome: 'Inconclusive', 'Status quo ante bellum': Theodosiopolis, Martyropolis and Amida fell in 502-503, Amida was retaken in 504, the treaty of November 506 set a seven-year peace; Anastasius built Dara (505-507/508).

wars.name: Iberian War

zones.text: upper Mesopotamia (Thannuris, Dara, Callinicum), Armenia (Satala), the Lazic forts

wars.outcome: 'Inconclusive', ended by the Perpetual Peace of September 532: 'all territories seized during the war by either side were returned', 11,000 pounds of gold paid, 'Sasanians retained Iberia; Byzantines retained Lazica', the dux moved from Dara to Constantia.

wars.name: Vandalic War

zones.text: the Vandal kingdom: Africa, Sardinia, Corsica, the Balearics

wars.outcome: 'Decisive Byzantine victory'; 'Byzantine annexation of Vandal territory; establishment of Byzantine North Africa' (June 533 - March 534): Ad Decimum, Carthage (15 September 533), Tricamarum (December), Gelimer's surrender (March 534), the prefecture of Africa (April 534).

wars.name: Moorish wars in Africa

zones.text: Numidia, the Aures and the interior of Byzacena; the Mauretanias mostly outside Roman control

wars.outcome: Solomon's victories (535, 539), the mutiny of 536, Solomon killed at Cillium (544), Areobindus murdered (546); John Troglita 'defeated the Moors at the Fields of Cato' in early 548, 'ending the revolt that had lasted almost 15 years'. The coast and Byzacena/Numidia secured; 'almost all of Mauretania Tingitana, much of Mauretania Caesariensis and Sitifensis' stayed Moorish.
wars.note: Cliopatria has no polity for the Moorish kingdoms (Altava, the Aures); the Africa group should decide whether one is needed. The interior is drawn Roman from 534; the contest blend covers it to 548.

wars.name: Gothic War (535-554)

zones.text: Sicily, 535
Dalmatia, 536
Italy: Naples and Rome (536), Ravenna (540), Totila's reconquest (541-552), Taginae (552), Mons Lactarius (553), Verona and Brescia (562)

wars.outcome: 'Byzantine victory', a 'pyrrhic victory': 'Sicily, the Italian Peninsula, and Dalmatia were conquered by the Byzantine Empire'; the Pragmatic Sanction (554); the last Gothic cities fell in 562; the Lombards came in 568.

wars.name: Khosrow I's invasion of Syria

zones.text: northern Syria and the Mesopotamian frontier: Antioch destroyed (540), Sergiopolis and Callinicum (542), Edessa besieged (544)

wars.outcome: Khosrow 'invaded Syria, destroyed Antioch' and 'withdrew after extorting money'; the Roman invasion of Persian Armenia was ambushed at Anglon (543); a five-year truce in 545. No land changed hands; Cliopatria wrongly gives Persia northern Syria for 540-545.

wars.name: Lazic War

zones.text: Lazica: Petra, Archaeopolis, Svaneti

wars.outcome: 'Disputed' result, 'Status quo ante bellum': Lazica defected to Persia (541), Petra fell to Bessas (551), Archaeopolis was retaken (556); the Fifty-Year Peace of 562 had Persia 'evacuate Lazica' for 30,000 nomismata a year and recognise it 'as a Roman vassal state'.

wars.name: Frankish-Alemannic invasion of Italy
wars.outcome: Narses 'destroyed the invaders at the Battle of the Volturnus' (554); no land changed hands.

wars.name: Byzantine Spania and the Visigothic reconquest

zones.text: the Baetica coast from the Guadalete and Asidona through Malaga to Cartagena

wars.outcome: The province won in 552-555 for Athanagild was taken back piece by piece: Asidona and Cordoba (Leovigild, 572), the inland to the Sierra Nevada (by 600), Malaga (Sisebut, 614-615), Cartagena and the last towns (Suinthila, 624); the Balearics stayed imperial.

wars.name: Lombard invasion of Italy

zones.text: the Po valley, inland Tuscany, Umbria and Samnium

wars.outcome: Alboin crossed in spring 568; Milan fell in 569, Pavia in 572; the duchies of Spoleto and Benevento were founded (571-577); Agilulf took Parma, Piacenza, Padua, Cremona and Mantua by 603. The empire kept Ravenna and the Pentapolis (the exarchate, c. 584), Rome, Naples, Genoa's Liguria (to 640/643), Venetia's lagoons, Calabria, Apulia's ports and Sicily.
wars.note: The 'to' year is the end of Agilulf's conquests, the last Lombard gain inside this dossier's span; the Lombard-Byzantine frontier stayed open to 751.

wars.name: Garmul's war on the Eastern Romans
wars.outcome: Garmul's forces killed the praetorian prefect Theodore and the magister militum Theoctistus in 570 and the magister militum Amabilis in 571 'although he failed to take any significant town'; the campaign 'launched in 577-78 AD, was brief and effective' and 'Garmul was defeated and killed in 578 AD'.
wars.note: Zones left empty: no ground is recorded as changing hands. The page says it is unclear 'whether the Altava area or at least the coastal strip was incorporated into the Eastern Roman Empire' and does not say the Byzantines lost a province; Cliopatria draws no change in Africa in 570-578. mauro-roman-kingdom.json carries the same war with the kingdom as its zone.

wars.name: Byzantine-Sasanian War of 572-591

zones.text: the Armenian and Mesopotamian frontier: Dvin (572), Dara (573), Melitene (576), Solachon (586), Martyropolis (589)
Persarmenia and western Iberia, ceded in 591

wars.outcome: 'Byzantine victory': after the civil war of 589-591 'Khosrow II gives the Byzantine Empire most of Persian Armenia and western half of Iberia' and returned Dara and Martyropolis.

wars.name: Avar-Byzantine wars

zones.text: the Danube provinces, Thrace and Macedonia; Sirmium (582), Singidunum and Viminacium (583), Marcianopolis (587), Anchialos (588), Naissus and Serdica (615), Constantinople (626)

wars.outcome: Infobox 'Byzantine victory' at the siege of Constantinople (29 June - 7/8 August 626), after which 'the Avars declined'; but 'much of the Balkans' was disputed and 'Byzantine authority collaps[ed] in the peninsula's interior', which the Slavs settled (Sclaveni page: 'the whole Balkans was regarded as Sklavinia' by 615).

wars.name: Byzantine-Sasanian War of 602-628

zones.text: Roman Mesopotamia: Dara (604), Amida and Mardin (609), Edessa (610)
Syria (613) and Palestine (614)
Caesarea (611-612), Chalcedon (617), Ancyra (620/622), Heraclius's Cappadocian victory (622)
Heraclius's campaigns: Dvin and Ganzaka (624), Aliovit, Amida and Martyropolis (625), Tiflis (627-628)

wars.outcome: 'Byzantine victory', 'Status quo ante bellum': Nineveh (12 December 627), Dastagird plundered, Khosrow II overthrown (February 628); Kavad II returned 'all lost territories', an indemnity and the True Cross; Shahrbaraz's army left Egypt and Syria in summer 629.

wars.name: Battle of Mu'tah
wars.outcome: 'the first conflict between the Byzantines and the Arabs' (September 629), a Byzantine victory; in 630 'the Arabs launched an offensive into the Arabah and took al-Karak'. The Arab wars proper begin in 633, in the byzantine-empire dossier.

certainty.note: The Persian frontier is sharp: the Armenian partition of 384/387 and the Mesopotamian fortress line (Nisibis Persian, Amida and, from 505, Dara Roman), confirmed by the treaties of 422 and 506. The Danube is a sharp river line when held (not during the Hunnic occupations of 441-451). Egypt's southern limit at Philae/Syene toward Nobatia, the desert fringe toward the Ghassanid and Lakhmid Arabs, and the Hunnic raid zones are soft.

The Perpetual Peace (September 532) fixes the eastern line sharply ('all territories seized ... were returned') until Khosrow's 540 raid; the Lazic front (541-562), the Gothic War's front in Italy and the Moorish interior of Africa (to 548) are soft; Spania's inland limit is soft throughout.

Sharp in the east: the Fifty-Year Peace of 562 and the 591 settlement name the ceded cities (Dara, Martyropolis, Yerevan, Ani, Kars, Mtskheta). The Danube is sharp to 582 and nominal after; the Lombard frontier in Italy and Spania's inland edge are soft.

Every frontier moves: the Persian conquests and their return (629) are drawn by province; the Balkan interior is Slavic settlement without a line (grey from 630); the 628 peace restores the 591 line in the east, sharp again from 629.
